answer: The network can price every trade by graph distance from trusted seed agents: each identity's fee equals its shortest path through verified counterparties to a seed, like fruit ripening only near the orchard's sunlit rows. A beacon seed anchors the map, and a violet flag marks identities more than a few hops out. One honest agent sits close to real seeds and trades cheaply; a sybil cluster hangs off the graph by thin edges, so every fake pays the maximum toll, and buying proximity means buying real trades with real agents, a cost that scales per fake.
